Now we’ve got a bit of new data from the local authority’s 2013/4 Strategic Transport Plan, which makes clear just how poor things were here before.
This report illustrates the challenges we face …
The analysis points out that people travelling by car currently account for around a third of all journeys to work (which is hardly an accident).
One out of every four trips can be accomplished through public transportation with adequate service.
Improvements in transportation ought to concentrate on decreasing dependence on vehicles rather than expanding their use.
But surely it wouldn’t make sense at all to build more roads? Why might these plans even worry us?
They fail to address improving road safety; every rise in traffic leads to a greater likelihood of accidents because it increases the number of travelers.
Recent studies have provided evidence for this phenomenon, which was first documented in the Traffic Engineering & Control journal one year ago. In fact, the authors conclude:
‘When road network conditions worsen or more vehicles enter congested roads […] both vehicle speed and travel time will also decrease [as indicated by slower response times]’
In other words, bad roads mean cars travelling at lower speeds.
What happens next? Well, studies looking into human reaction times show that the longer it takes someone to get behind the wheel, the less certain they feel, leading them to pull back off the roadway for fear of hitting another car and causing further delays. At some point a tipping point will kick in where the delay is too great, meaning drivers lose confidence completely and choose not to hit the throttle, resulting in gridlock through increased stopping distances…
If this sounds complicated, let me go over it again with very simple language.
Longer, busier roads lead to accidents, which slow down traffic due to feared collisions. Drivers react more slowly which causes even worse problems, culminating in cities becoming places where no-one wants to live unless they’re totally obsessed with money.
That doesn’t sound like something you’d want your city to be. Let’s look at what might actually help fix our problem instead…
Commuting by bike

5 How Much Space Do I Need for Bathroom Remodels?
It's only human nature to want your house to feel comfortable and inviting when you walk into it. One aspect of making your house look more attractive is renovating the kitchen or bath area. However, if you're unsure where, how much or why you should invest in remodeling an existing space, take heart. There are things that can be done with little expense but get dramatic results. Additionally, most homeowners don't need all-inclusive renovators; it's possible to revitalize an old room without breaking the bank.
To enhance the guest-friendly ambiance during kitchen or bathroom renovations, incorporate furniture, light fixtures, and other decorative elements aimed at encouraging interaction with newly installed countertops, cabinets, tiles, or floorings. The key to creating ambiance isn't necessarily spending big on expensive design elements. A few inexpensive items such as picture frames, wall knobs, lighted hooks, glass or copper coasters, mirrors and plant stands add character -- while keeping costs down. In fact, some items may already be around if they were part of your original decorating scheme when you moved into your house.
No matter what type of remodel you're considering, start by addressing every room's needs first before moving on to any areas you'd like to improve upon later on. Older renovations often result in kitchens and bathrooms having multiple leftover features that make reinstallation simpler compared to starting with new items. Doing this also helps prevent clutter buildup, which can detract significantly from personal appearance. For example, removing unnecessary hanging lamps (including overhead lights) saves valuable visual real estate from view unless needed again.

As one way of avoiding overdoing it so quickly at the beginning of a project, then, proceed like this: Create spaces with simple things like buckets filled with sand, mason jars containing pebbles or leaves, wooden boxes holding flowers or toys. Then put away those extra pots and pans, light switches, wires, etc., until after everything else around them has been completed. These items remain hidden when unused; thus reducing any negative associations they may have with those rooms for potential future projects requiring their presence.

The following tips will help you focus on what matters most:

* Focus primarily on the actual work rather than looking forward to how everything looks afterwards.

A new device developed by researchers at Monash University in Australia employs an integrated 3D sensor system known as SfM (Structure From Motion). This system utilizes two RGB cameras positioned at various points on the smartphone along with a monochrome infrared camera to calculate depth information.

The SfM chip is based on software algorithms similar to those used in smartphones today for detecting objects like fingers. Once it determines depth information, it takes photos of faces or areas of interest and displays them as temperature maps with various colors representing high or low temperatures.

After developing this algorithm over four years, they could prove their ability through real testing during World Rugby Championship held in Dunedin in early December. Wearing smart goggles, participants took part in the tests that included sensors.

Our system overlays temperature data onto thermal images to allow security staff to identify individuals regardless of whether they're wearing glasses. Said lead researcher Michael Kifer.


The engineers devised strategies that enabled them to recognize individuals in busy areas by integrating computer-vision techniques like texture identification, color assessment, and light measurement into a newly developed software technology. This approach allowed for location tracking of crowds, comprehensive gathering scrutiny, and precise person counting without requiring visual assistance. This also included recognizing whether they were standing still, running, dancing, etc.
Kifer explained further, “With traditional methods, security staff have to man a moving guard tower to look out for suspects.”

This technology will be eventually available for commercial use. However, developers don’t expect it to be popularized until phones reach a higher resolution and manufacturers start releasing affordable devices that feature advanced capabilities such as dual display, ML (Machine Learning), AR/VR, XDA-Developers

With each new release and model come many upgrades and improvements, including more storage space for your data plus a longer time between when it'll be overwritten under certain circumstances. Not only does this make the new releases more attractive than ever, it also means the old ones have become almost obsolete if they aren't already. There comes a point where no one will even bother to support older hardware anymore -- unless that hardware is preserved.
All of which is why we are so excited to offer this post from Red Hat in its entirety. Clonezilla, also known as CloneFS, offers this feature: it allows you to create a copy of your entire system onto an external storage device like a hard drive. Unlike other systems designed solely for backing-up purposes, most systems that do a lot of system management don't really need to be copied around; all the information resides inside them as files anyway. To maintain an exact duplicate of data stored entirely on disk, you can use CloneFS effectively.
There is NO WAY to backup linux using DOS commands (no alternative command lines either for example such as dos2unix).
Good news, though... I'm going to first explain what exactly "backup" implies. Then we will look into some options, based on what potential needs you may have. Let's go!
What's A Backed-Up?
Before digging into any specific ways of backing-up Linux operating systems, let me explain what the actual problem entails here: "Backing up."
Many people often use these two words interchangeably, meaning by "backing up" they want a complete set of files that is able to be restored later – essentially creating copies of their primary OS files on another storage device(s). They don't want to just change locations on an external volume or use different format types. Despite its common usage, "backup" in reality refers to something distinct from what it signifies.
Backups, aside from being used more frequently to merely refer to a transfer method rather than simply having been used before, specifically imply a number of benefits beyond just transferring files, namely:
• Being able to restore multiple times without fear of losing anything
• Being able to access files during periods of downtime
• Be able to alter important files during the process of restoration (when necessary to correct an error)
How Does Backup Work?
Backup refers to a set of procedures typically integrated into bigger practices like DRP (Disaster Recovery Planning) and DRMs (Disaster Recovery Management). It has several requirements, generally including:
• Storage of backed up data - Usually through RAID array, sometimes online backups, etc.
• User-friendly interface - On a separate machine or through Web browser console
• Availability - 24/7 uptime so there is always a consistent view of data intact.
When talking about using command-line tools for backup, take note that none of this applies since it requires constant maintenance efforts, changes in permissions, etc.

Saint Swithun may have been associated with her due to his support of Southhampton, England, where there is also a shrine dedicated to her. Elsewhere another saint also named St Swithun and recognised by his moniker was in Italy!
According to legend St Swithun (born sometime between 580-601), was the son of Prince Edwin of Bernicia who died or was strangled during a rebellion against Danish rule when St Swithun was young. He fled into exile somewhere near to Northumbria, probably to keep safe from the Danes. However, King Oswald sent him back to the area from whence he came to help restore peace to Northumberland. When Oswald subsequently met and married Princess Idonea, daughter of Echtraeth-Sweyn, king of Kent, they both travelled together to meet their wedding gifts from the Danes. One of these presents was the head of a young Dane chained up within the latticed gates of York Minster.
He was widely esteemed in Northumbria after being ordained as a bishop and subsequently requesting his own confirmation. During the reign of Penda of Mercia this split the kingdom in two, and when Swithun returned from the south east with the newly crowned Charles Martel he stood at odds with the king himself. Penda was defeated on several fronts and Swithun fought alongside his rival in a famous battle near Glangwili mountain in Anglesey where the king won according to legend. There ensued a contentious civil strife regarding Illtyd's succession, which later gave rise to another conflict between Hywel Dda and Owain from Vortigern's court.
When Swithun retired from the priesthood and politics he took refuge on the Isle of Wight in honour of St Augustine before finally settling at Gloucester as Abbot of Alchester Abbey. Sadly, despite all his efforts to help Christianity rise amongst the Celts of Britain, the religious turmoil led him to leave England again. A budget was passed that aims to repeal the privatization of alcohol sales in Pennsylvania. The measure -- H.B. 3387 -- has been approved by the Democratic leadership and is awaiting passage from the GOP-controlled minority, said State Rep. Ken Bonior, D-Pennsburg, who serves as chair of the Appropriations Committee for the lower chamber. Altria Group Inc., a company that produces Marlboro cigarettes, has approached Bonior's caucus for potential sales of alcohol licenses since last year, but no agreements have been reached yet.
"Their interest, if we were to tap into them like that, wouldn't be good enough," he added. "We don't want another monopoly here."
Speaker Dennis Jolly, representing Republicans in Vanderbilt, stated that lawmakers on both sides support the fundamental concept of the proposal, yet they disagree about details like price points and licensing regulations. (Republicans streamline application processes.) Republican fiscal analyst David Weyrich estimates privatizing alcohol sales could generate about $79 million a year in revenue per year and create dozens of jobs.
According to records compiled by the Penn Distillers industry trade group, 43 brands are currently available for purchase in Pennsylvania. Private labeling products make up more than one-half of those offerings: One company, called GiGi's Liquor, produces a total of 814 different types of liquor and beer under multiple labels. About four percent of alcohol sold in Pennsylvania today takes customers to private labeling venues; most other bottles go through wholesalers or retailers like Giant Eagle or Whole Foods.
Under the proposal being considered, out-of-state manufacturers would compete against each other at wholesale stores to offer new branded options, while local producers would continue to operate their own shops within the state. Because no change is expected to affect prices for consumers, Bonior said the law needs to be quick-tracked so the process starts straightaway after an executive order creating the board responsible for overseeing implementation can be issued later in January. Bonior said a similar strategy for selling tobacco products was successfully put in place three years ago, resulting in a hiring freeze and increased competition among sellers of electronic cigarettes, cigars, nicotine patches and e-cigarettes.

I guess during my nearly three months in Hong Kong since leaving Merrill Lynch, I'd become far too comfortable being surrounded by traders; my new job requires a lot less human interaction. Being around people in perpetual fear of losing money these days is remarkable because it's hard to get yourself out of business troughs now without looking foolish for having guessed wrong or trying too hard all along. Investors have been warned again and again through countless articles, TV spots and web sites to keep investing in any given sector in hopes of getting some kind of positive return from the crash—and it turned out not to be so simple or black-and-white after all. Even today, I intend to seek signs of hope while avoiding an excessive concentration solely on possible scenarios.

The best way I have found to inspire my own leadership development is through contemplation and introspection about myself as a leader. I've been cultivating these personal strengths over many years, beginning with leadership traits that emerged naturally from childhood and adolescence before I formally learned more sophisticated skills on the job.
Studies indicate that proficient professionals often adopt either a behavioral management strategy (whereby employees adhere to directives set by their supervisors) or authoritative leadership practices.
But to be effective today's top performers also must show what we call "self-leadership," which means managing themselves first before directing others toward shared objectives.
Like most good ideas, this notion has its roots in research showing that human beings are born both competent and curious – two universal features common across all cultures that exist through all stages of life.
Where constructive problem-solving kicks off is when it reaches the unique stage where every person actively contributes to making sense out of situations encountered in unexpected ways or requiring creative solutions. That's because humans instinctively seek meaning and understanding - for themselves, each other, our communities and the planet we live upon.
This inner drive animates not only the religious/spiritual/philosophical traditions of humanity but also contemporary scientific findings attesting to brain activity related to empathy, cooperation, helping others, purpose, passion ... or what some psychologists refer to as an intrinsic motivation that drives exploration and discovery without any external rewards attached! How lucky we are that those attributes continue to grow stronger as time marches forward!
Life’s challenges often present us with opportunities for growth if we choose wisely. When I contemplate who I am, whom I serve and what I aspire to accomplish, these questions arise within me.
I'm grateful for my experiences so far, grateful for friends like you whose kindred spirits bring such warmth into my heart every day. We work hard together, laughing along the way.
And yet here's what keeps coming back to me again: The ultimate value lies not just in doing things; it's in doing them right, honestly and transparently. Because ultimately that's what makes us whole people.
To achieve success, embrace the courage to make bold moves with no fear of outcomes; seek wisdom by reflecting on errors; persevere in pursuit of goals regardless of setbacks until positive results occur at least once! - Karen McCauley, CEO Karen McCauley Consultancy Inc.

Partisan divides Americans.
This divide was evident most starkly in 2017 when Republicans and Democrats used data differently following Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to a Gallup survey. Polls taken just three days before Election Day showed vastly different expectations for Donald Trump as compared with the national averages at publication day: Democrats predicted he would lose by about 3% whereas Republicans expected him to win by roughly two percentage points. When those polls were published shortly after polling day, Democratic expectations for his re-election had dropped significantly but Republican predictions remained largely unchanged – despite considerable gains among Democrats and losses among GOP voters.
This division between Republicans and Democrats reflects broader divisions, especially within each party itself. Democrats are generally less critical of statistical accuracy and its importance compared to Republicans. The partisan gap is magnified because individuals are likely to view statistics selectively or use them only where convenient.
Partisans use historical records and other sources to support political claims. Such evidence is often biased in favor of certain viewpoints by excluding contradictory data. In addition, many people feel pressured to conform to societal norms rather than simply stating the facts under discussion.
This trend toward groupthink raises difficulties not just among policymakers and public officials who rely on statistics for decision-making but also American society more broadly. Political disagreement based upon inaccurate information fuels polarization over policy issues like climate change while increasing distrust of elected representatives; all factors that contribute to low voter turnout.
To improve trust in elections, policymakers must recognize that there needs to be agreement across the electorate about basic principles of democracy; this begins with viewing statistical truthfulness as an essential virtue worthy of respect by citizens. Additionally, programs designed specifically to address current concerns surrounding election integrity may need to target more nuanced audiences who do not want broad-based reforms involving changes in voting laws or methods which could cause confusion among voters regardless of party affiliation.

Indeed, numerous cases are recorded by historians regarding occurrences in the United States. history where elected officials and powerful interests used misleading statistics to justify policies that later proved harmful. Here are a few notable cases:

- During World War I, President Woodrow Wilson claimed that Germany's submarine warfare against merchant ships violated international law and required military action. However, research showing that these attacks took place during peacetime suggests otherwise. Wilson later apologized for his mistake, though the damage inflicted was already done.

- After Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans in 2005, Governor Kathleen Blanco faced criticism from local activists who criticized government spending plans for rebuilding her state. However, Blanco defended her decisions citing projections from the Census Bureau that overstated population growth estimates, leading to higher-than-needed allocations for FEMA response efforts.

For example, let’s consider what the scientific consensus predicted back in September 1987 regarding global warming, when researchers were studying how much carbon dioxide could be safely added to our atmosphere. My predecessor, Kevin Trenberth, was by that time a meteorologist working as part of World Weather and Climate Research Group (now NOAA), which makes life easier if you have colleagues named Kevin Trenberth; that kind of friendliness is hard to find in any other field.
Back in September 1987, there were really only two models with real future projections left in the game: GISS, the Global Institute of Sustainability in New York (my institution now), and Hadley, in the U.K.

Roberts and Mary Ann Walker were each awarded an award for volunteering with the community centre for more than five years. Lou says she was first inspired by her mother's example.
"I started working in the kitchen at my mum's house when I was just old enough to help wash dishes," she recalled. "I thought it would be fun doing something different from what I'd been used to." Lou now has a career as an operator on cruise ships and is still going strong with the community centre - so good that it gave her a complete beginners certificate in cooking.
Tammy joined the team as an office manager 30 years ago, helping organise activities such as roadshows. She also joined the Big Event team and organised one of the biggest arts competitions ever held in Port Augusta.
As an executive board member and committee member, Reita volunteered for multiple boards throughout her career, serving as president for four consecutive years! Despite her hectic schedule filled with numerous holiday trips away from her hometown, she never missed an event since she appreciated the consistent opportunities for volunteering time.
Mary Anne has had a long history connecting the community centre back to its roots in Port Adelaide. When she took up the position of co-ordinator, she was backed up with the passion of others keen to get involved and support the centre. They include her husband Don, Fran Westgarth, Heather Taylor and Phil Robertson. Through their efforts, they managed to get a new scholarship into school for some children and helped improve elderly people's lives as well.
The other ten volunteers were likewise recognized with commendations as well. Their achievements are also worthy of praise. The full list below shows some of the other awards given out - plus some details about how the nominees were chosen. If you're interested in learning more or becoming even more involved yourself, why not come along to a future event? You may only need to put your name down once!
The Community Centre runs six weekday events which cater for ages 3+ during term-time – plus a weekly story time every Monday (9am). Our main cafe features freshly-baked buns, muffins and cakes made from scratch using wholesome ingredients, served with homemade cheese, jam and honey. We also sell food vouchers priced at $2.98, great to hand out to families. Volunteers embrace the opportunity to participate actively - particularly when they can offer additional financial contributions for costs such as cake rentals and gift bag supplies.
Through our program, we offer art workshops during both terms and on Saturday's Art Days, featuring guest artists and plenty of engaging activities outdoors. We also do lots of fundraising….for things like scholarships for local kids, car parks, swimming pool upgrades, furniture, pots & pans, kites… and anything else we're asked for. We understand everyone has their own priorities……but we believe the bigger picture should involve making life better for those living around here.

records of former inmates from voting rolls, further undermining public trust in our democracy and a key component for voters’ right to exercise their franchise.
In his first 10 days as governor, Cuomo ordered all county clerks across the state to remove any voter registration information for felons or ex-felons living in supervised housing facilities or halfway houses from lists held online by Department of Motor Vehicles.
When pressed on this policy changes yesterday at an event commemorating Holocaust survivor Anne Frank’s 85th birthday, Cuomo didn’t respond when asked whether he believed the new order was “fair,” but he did say there were caseworkers involved in removing people’s names from the list, adding that they had been providing them notice.
That may have been true yesterday, but officials from many law enforcement agencies told me they haven’t seen such notices yet. Much less did the New York State Legislature recently pass a measure establishing clear procedures for voters who want to challenge registrations based on felony convictions.
What does this mean for voters?
It means that one in three black men ages 26 to 34 are disenfranchised under current laws. That’s about half of black male civic participation compared to just over two-thirds among white male civic participation; more than twice as many Natives lose their rights to vote each year after committing a misdemeanor crime. It also means that under existing laws more than 9% of registered Democrats and more than 7% of Republican voters will now be unable to cast ballots because they’ve lost their citizenship.
The commonwealth should protect citizens’ right to freely express their views through elections, not undermine it. This is particularly painful because people convicted of nonviolent offenses like possession of narcotics or simple assault rarely commit crimes again. Felonies constitute merely a minuscule portion of total criminal convictions.
Despite minimal discussion within both the Assembly and Senate, these administrative measures were successfully enacted. The Assembly voted 33-to-14 last month on a bill authored by Democratic Assemblywoman Donna Lupardo authorizing removal of voter files from DMV’s website following completion of probation. She refuses to explain why her bill doesn’t go into effect immediately, even though some counties already removed data from websites within weeks of sentencing, according to its lead sponsor and the secretary of State’s office.
Lupardo also failed to ask lawmakers how enforcement might affect those on parole or probation. I don’t think she intended this course of action to be irreversible, but there is little protection against a future change in administration or potentially retroactive application if voters file a lawsuit.

ULIP products offer investment options with better returns than bank fixed deposits, which can easily yield 3% or more on maturity. However, these plans usually do not pay dividend yields higher than bank schemes as they aim at maintaining an equity share allocation of at least 10% under all investment options available for the policy cover (a significant percentage). The main attraction of this product over traditional loans against investments (L&I) policies lie in their ability to manage taxes better and allow flexibility in fund choices based on various life-cycle stages, combined with tax benefits. Also, while banks ensure that there is only one option after five years from the date of purchase, ULIP holders can choose between different types of units such as equity-linked, unit linked and pure savings type- along with several low-risk alternatives like government debentures and bonds.
Investors should expect high premium growth irrespective of which year you purchase your policy; it's the same if bought before or after 2019 fiscal end. However, if purchased in January 2020 and held till February-end, starting April 2020 policyholders will enjoy double pension benefit including interest earned on both ends of the loan agreement. Those who invest early in January stand to receive higher interest rates due to these investments typically enjoying longer tenures compared to other accounts, as reported by Bankrate.com.
You should know about Tax implications before purchasing an LIC policies. Up to Rs. 5,000 monthly, premium payments can be deducted from income tax without any additional tax liability; however, above this amount, additional taxes apply. Thereafter, if an individual dies within 18 months following initial contribution into annuity scheme then no payment would come out. If multiple beneficiaries claim entitlements then lower age group members hold priority until death of eldest beneficiary occurs. Since current premium waiver feature stated for all term life policies remains applicable unless specified otherwise, so consider taking care while drafting documentation & signing agreements related to such documents prior appointment. Keep in mind that even though we name them differently but everyone knows what is Corporate Pension Plan and Government Employees' Pension Scheme right? Even though both plans fall under social security heads still they work separately from each other hence both must not taken together at once because there could occur conflicts among them resulting into wastage of funds meant for public sector employees whereas individuals belonging to private entities may find some favour when it comes down to sharing surplus profits amongst themselves instead of spending money elsewhere. It boils down to whether governments decide to implement new rules mandating minimum wage increase every three years over next six years or let existing norms prevail unchanged. According to legend, long ago, King Solomon entrusted two maids who had been sent by him to a devout Jewish woman named Hagith. She regarded them as her daughters-in-law and offered them the best welcome they could receive because the king supervised the kitchen staff.
One day the women, feeling quite bored while waiting for King Solomon’s return from foreign travel, agreed to help one another pick herbs from the garden. Their intention was to pray and sing hymns to thank God for his blessings.

But the two leaders’ views are not mutually exclusive; they can be expressed without attacking each other personally. Indeed, if we were to combine their points of view and ask each to summarize them once more in one sentence each as outtakes from our current debates, they would come up with this:
Macron: It’s time for European unity!
Trump: We the people want America first! We succeed through free trade and open borders, yet we should bear the responsibility!
This simple summary makes clear how both parties share some basics. Both believe strongly that citizens of their countries should speak out fairly in their government’s affairs. Both believe their governments should work hard to serve all its citizens equally rather than favoring the rich and powerful. Both see themselves leading peoples toward a prosperous future, though they differ over which path that journey will take. Although the descriptions vary considerably, both approaches focus on allocating resources—such as taxes—to construct a country's infrastructure—a variety of projects including roads, bridges, highways, tunnels, sewage systems, air-traffic control facilities, and electrical distribution networks—aiming to generate employment opportunities with higher wages and greater profitability.
What does this tell us?
It tells me that these vastly dissimilar political blocs have far more common sense behind them than I had imagined. Perhaps there is hope after all.
Far too oftentimes, our heated ideological shouting matches in Washington City pits the left against the right, like groups in battle camps, shooting across the lines at one another instead of working together to help resolve a problem. Striving for results worth striving for requires thinking freely enough to get away from personal animosity. When we selected Tivo HD as a portable streaming solution for replacing our cable service, we felt thrilled. We were disappointed, though, with how slow the process was, especially because it could only connect to certain channels through Internet Explorer with the tablet connected to Wi-Fi. But then along comes TabletTV. Once we set up the app for the first time in our home theater setup around Thanksgiving 2014, it really ran smooth after the fact.

Should you find this feature not supported in your area currently, revisit regularly for updates on potential expansion of partner networks. You’ll notice that at least nine companies are currently listed as compatible with the service, which should get you going pretty easily even without access to Verizon FiOS.
TabletTV works by making use of multiple input ports within the device itself. When you plug your Blu-ray player into one of those inputs, sets a picture source, and launches Apple AirPlay or Google Chromecast, the service allows you to start playing a live video or download a show recording straight to your television. If you have a USB port, too — which many tablets also include — the service allows you to directly stream shows onto your television.
The price for getting all this functionality depends on what packages you’re interested in signing up for. The monthly subscription fees vary from $9.95 to $13.95, according to your spending preference per month. Since it requires both a Bluetooth headset and a smartphone to run properly, you can choose either a limited plan ($13.95 per month) or a more extensive monthly package that gives you unlimited access to any streaming content included in your choice of plans ($17.95 per month). Alternatively, you may opt to buy a one-year membership rather than paying monthly; there are also weekly and bi-weekly options at reduced rates. For example, rather than pay $9.95 per month for an average monthly package that would cover things like streaming Netflix or YouTube videos, you can save almost $60 annually by picking up the five-month trial offer for $87, or select the “Save Big” option for only $55.95. There’s something for everyone, no matter whether you become a TabletTV member once, twice, or often during your entertainment journey.

Why is everyone so excited by vegetarianism?
Why Don’t Vegans Eat Meat, Milk or Dairy?
Let’s start with the idea that vegans aren’t humans who don’t want to kill animals. I’m just going to say it out loud: They do.
There is no such thing as an animal-free human. We make proteins through DNA, which comes from animals. We also use milk, eggs and other goods we obtain directly from animals. If you have no objection to supporting cows, pigs, or chickens, then what reason do you have for choosing not to? You need them like they need you.
What About the Nutritional Diets Of Vegetarians, Vegans & Their Friend, The Fruitarian?
Kicking back on delicious fruits is one of life's pleasures. But there is a lot more behind these delectable choices than simply eating without killing people. When you cut your diet down to only plant foods and supplements, nutrition starts to suffer. Fitness levels and disease risks are jeopardized simultaneously.

Through this procedure, significant improvements in pediatric urinary tract surgeries have been achieved.
In most cases, children are born with either a ureterocele - which is undescended urine through the renal pelvis into the abdominal cavity - or ureteropelvic junction obstruction (UPJO), where there is inadequate drainage between the kidney and the ureter due to a blockage caused by narrowing at the junction of the ureter with the renal pelvis. Both conditions can develop before birth but they typically present as urinary incontinence requiring prolonged catheterization once babies are walking. Infants without proper care will need lifelong support, such as regular bladder drainage through catheters or frequent surgeries throughout their lifetime.

OAKLAND (AP) — When Major League Baseball opens a season in Japan, count on the Oakland Athletics to show up. The regular season will start at the Tokyo Dome for the fifth time on Wednesday, and this is the third time in a row that the A’s will be playing at a ballpark with an audience of at least 40,000.
Even when it was just the three-time-runners-up team from the American League West last spring, they put together their best stretch of baseball of the year winning two games against New York in September.
Stippling's work at Oakland for over six years is expected to increase this unrecognized club's popularity.
The Athletics are advancing in their quest for veteran pitching assistance through free agency. They traded for lefty Zach Greinke on July 31 despite him being off the books for about two years; he signed a $92 million deal worth four years with the Athletics.
Moving ahead though are things like finding hitters who can be above-average contributors but won’t break records and looking to keep adding depth around designated hitters Dan Straily and Brett Anderson through the normal process.
Alongside them will be cash-strapped teams such as Philadelphia and Kansas City, and the new competition would hopefully force magnanimous owners like Randa Bannister and George Zlotoff to think outside the box in order to remain competitive.
For example, if the Royals sign another slugger beyond Mike Moustakas then it could be a long road back to contention without changing owner David Ogilvy’s views down the middle-field fence. And even if they do change ownership — which isn’t unlikely — the club may need to sell a piece of its farm system to play catch up with the higher-end market in Los Angeles or San Francisco.
But nothing will really happen unless Bannister and Zlotoff take matters into their own hands via strategic moves. We’ll see how both clubs navigate their own struggles. But there is one thing that is rather certain: Stippling is going to make sure his club shows no signs of giving away.
Still, it seems as though the organization is preparing for the day when it becomes less important in terms of simply making winners out of mediocre players instead of getting better ones. That line should definitely not exist anymore by the time pitchers and outfielders hit the field for the first time in October. After all, baseball in Japan doesn’t belong here.

One example is KAT-2. Its primary function will be establishing precision communications among forces across the spectrum of operations. As part of this effort, it looks to transform military wireless services by supporting soldiers’ ever-increasing need to communicate globally with advanced multimedia devices such as cell phones, laptops and portable computers. This includes creating effective methods for transmitting ultra high-definition video feeds between units in theater and anywhere else with a reliable connection. For the Navy or Marine Corps, these advancements can be particularly valuable when deployed at sea, where bandwidth limitations make it difficult not only to sustain vital tactical mechanisms but also to keep soldiers connected to their families back home. The potential impacts are astounding. Consider: Within 30 minutes, thousands of soldiers could see pictures of loved ones via satellite TV. Much more important, they’d be able to chat with them virtually in real time via instant messaging. That’s a scenario that would transform the entire concept of ‘family’ when deployed overseas. And those who work below decks might find themselves with access to TVs depicting family members enjoying what life means back at home—realistic television images that help inspire soldiers’ resolve in battle while keeping morale up at base camp.
KAT-2 maintains an essential role that extends beyond simply relaying images. One of the crucial elements contributing to "the force multiplier effect" involves expanding the influence of air, ground, and maritime forces beyond what a single branch could achieve individually. We’re not talking about extra planes or more tanks, though that would add to our ability to project our power as well. Rather, it's referring to the fact that a small fraction of highly efficient technology is available now—and quickly gaining efficiencies—to enable forces operating abroad to be simultaneously more effective and less costly overall. Increased demand for high-resolution optics for infantry scouts, unmanned platforms, and their integration with drones drives growing fatigue in ammunition supplies compared to past situations.
All of this represents significant progress. While no solution can yet fully replace conventional warfare forces, rapid advances continue to improve decision-making processes in ways previously unavailable. New technologies allow commanders to monitor events happening hundreds of miles away without even being physically present. In urban environments like Somalia, KAT-2 provides unparalleled mobile connectivity within the dense confines of crowded cities, enabling Marines to keep secure contact with friends, family and command centers across the globe. Despite acknowledging the inherent danger in regions such as Mogadishu and Kareri in Somalia, KAT-2 provides a sense of security, one which commanders do not fully comprehend until they have successfully landed back at their base camp.

X-Scanner
McAfee sells X-Scanner products that detect and respond to attacks such as SQL injection; e-mail-based attacks; malware; network intrusions; viruses; system administrators' misconfigurations; password thefts; key loggers; fileless infections; social engineering; dodgy website content; theft of intellectual property; phishing; spoofing; data loss prevention; user environment issues like: zero-day vulnerabilities; and other types of attacks.
The product is widely used by a significant user base, with approximately one billion users globally - this represents a notable increase of over 60% compared to the previous year and significantly surpasses the sales made by McAfee in 2003.
But before you go running out to buy your bag of Ghostbusters supplies (or whatever your preferred "Ghostbuster" brand may be), keep in mind that McAfee has a lot more selling to do before it reaches full market share.
The New York Times reports:
Strictly speaking, in most cases McAfee's antivirus software does not actually kill or eliminate any virus or worm. Instead, its software forces computers infected with malicious programs to remain disconnected from the Internet so they can't spread their code further....[i]f McAfee's strategy works, though, it could lead both companies into mutually beneficial alliances by exposing weaknesses in users' systems while keeping those systems visible until they're rebuilt... The videos showed an overweight father with little time in his hands taking his six-year-old son onto the Guangzhou subway. During the five-minute journey to his home — longer than most metro journeys you can take in China (which also helps explain why some people argue that this video has political overtones) – he didn't lose one cent. And that's because it was just another day for Lu Jiahao, who makes 30 times what the average worker does every month by putting money aside into a company called Yingxiong International Logistics Group Limited.

Well, Lu isn't an ordinary guy: he runs the country's biggest online P2P lender, Global Qiankun, its shares have zoomed nearly three-fold since mid-February as Mr Lu took advantage of demand, buying up more capital to fund future expansion. In fact, so much demand exists among foreign private-equity firms and funds potentially shorting the stock that they are now worried about "China bubbles".

So far, these fears haven't impacted the value of Qiankun shares; it's only recently that those shorts have started investing through margin accounts. But if things get worse there is certainly room to run with Wang Yanlin's story. He may be lying behind the scenes, but he really holds all the power.

And this recent development points out a huge danger.

The scheme threatens to drive away those foreigners thinking about getting involved. They believed that Qingyun might fall due to overexpenditure, heavy debt, or both before encountering financial difficulties. It seems anyone looking abroad at P2P platforms should think twice given what's happening right here in China.

After all, let us remember how the P2P industry developed. Back in early 2014, four companies offered loans to people without any guarantee except their own personal credit histories. Initially, people gained profits through investment, but soon their capital was depleted due to rapid consumption of funds from fresh investments. Despite financial struggles, other platforms emerged as well.

Due to the absence of shareholders, these entities relied on their client's savings rather than selling bonds. Hundreds of millions of yuan poured in, resulting in panic selling among their customers and a complete collapse later that year.
With luck, the same thing won't happen in Beijing. I'm sure the authorities will impose greater oversight; it's hard to see them back down once spectacular failures occur as often they do around the world. That said, they won't necessarily stop short of ruining businesses and crushing entire industries where the risks aren't too high. Indeed, they seem determined to keep trying until they succeed.
But the problem with foreign direct investment, particularly into high-tech sectors, is that it could lead to a lot of pain in the long term. Investors simply don't know when the next big failure might come along and kill the weak link in their stack.
This is not to say that Chinese startups are inherently safer than foreign ones. But they're usually going to cost less money initially than Western

What does a county manager actually do?
In addition to being responsible for overseeing countywide operations, most managers also direct the hiring and firing of key personnel, budgeting, contract management, legal affairs, purchasing activities, staff development and human relations. County managers frequently assist in resolving problems reported by citizens via county councils or committees. Finally, they ensure compliance with laws affecting county business, like contracts and zoning ordinances.

Where does the concept of a successful genocide stem from?
It is interesting how both these stories became associated with the genocide in our minds today. However, when looking back at historical events many years ago, they didn't seem so black and white... about "the iron hand" she was going to apply, which has led her critics on down through history into some rather harsh words.

Her successor David Cameron followed up with an equally tough tack when he took office last year - parting ways with the European Union, separating from Scotland, getting rid of much of the remaining tax credit system, ending free movement of labour between members states, slashing welfare costs, signing off huge deregulatory measures, reducing government spending, putting back regulations where there are now loopholes... you name it.

And yet, here we are at mid-August 2013 - having been promised one thing after another for four and a half years by Mr Cameron, despite all his self-promotion, trying every conceivable tactic to get hold of popular support, whether PR, PR or people power.

What happened? A lot more than France might have done, Mind you, due to military intervention (so maybe not quite a failure).

But why do we keep voting away our most capable leaders, over and over again?

Mr Cameron said genuinely that he felt sorry for those who had voted Leave and wanted to listen, but many experts think the gap between reality and perception has grown ever wider since then.

The traditional way of making sense of this phenomenon is to assume that voters' views of their leaders were always pretty accurate, until very recently. No doubt they were - if they ever could be - because at least a little experience was involved.

But isn't it possible that today's British public - both voters and politicians alike - are so disenchanted with politics these days, and have such negative feelings about its institutions and personalities generally, that any politician can ride roughshod across them?

An increasingly angry, sceptical electorate may be unimpressed by promises, wishful thinking or clever spin. But what if they don't believe even the simple things like 'three years from now I will take responsibility for my own destiny'? Or 'Britain is better place than France?'

Suddenly, being defeated seems a hell of a lot less frightening; sacrifice and hardship seem no longer so necessary to be believed to be worthwhile sacrifices.

As long as it looks like winning, winning becomes everything. The Labour leader Ed Miliband pointed out yesterday:

"Staying true to your principles does pay dividends."

But what if what matters isn't paying dividends, but simply staying true? Indeed, Britain must strive to achieve unity more vigorously.

Or what if what matters isn't so much ideas as feeling worthwhile?

It's unlikely that politics will ever be perfect. We'll need to start holding ourselves accountable. And we need to learn to acknowledge ourselves as losers sometimes, in order to remain winners in the end. In return we shall receive comfort from knowing we are doing something positive anyway. Let us ponder what the future may hold, especially when considering the approaching election.

But this was not enough to keep CNN’s Valeria Cappelletti on board. “We’ve got something new here,” she said during her press conference yesterday at an Ottawa media event for her new book A Very Short History of Political Satire. “It doesn’t have to be perfect or clever. Sometimes it just has to tickle your funny bone.” Her first full-length satirical look at politics aims to help non-Canadians understand what all the fuss is about.
With its casual tone, pop culture reference (everything from Star Trek to Harry Potter to Justin Bieber) and amusing anecdotes tied to current events – then-senator John Ibbitson tweeting his doubts about the success of Conservative ticket-collector Kip Freeland — the book is bound to hit home with the uninitiated. “I thought it would appeal to people who don’t know anything about us but who want to learn a little bit,” Cappelletti says with a smile.
In order to do so, she added lists containing: Who is a journalist in Canada? Why some Canadians are so obsessed with gender equality? Why we call our prime minister Mr. Harper? And What makes a Canadian frivolous? The sections provide insightful examination of Canadian behavior - familiar tropes, if you'll allow it.
Politicians often find their witty comments overshadowed by dark humor in the political sphere.
“When you’re making fun of us it feels like we were part of the problem when we did it ourselves,” Cappelletti says. “Because we laugh too hard about things when other people walk into meetings without looking over their shoulders wondering if cameras are rolling.” It seems worthwhile giving politicians back the power of levity. After all — wouldn’t we have more of a chance to get involved if we were laughing along? [caption id="attachment_5798" align="aligncenter" width="600"]Capeletti image[/caption]

though the Beachwood, Ohio corporation has a 30-year record of making fitness products, its main attraction is to get you involved with choirs as it becomes your new favorite exercise.
This month, a fitness center opened in the newly constructed Westlake Village Shopping Center, measuring 30,000 square feet, situated on Beachwood Avenue between Lakewood Boulevard and Interstate-480. The facility was meticulously planned over several years before its grand opening.
Corus' annual membership cost starts at $129 for one year's access to three workstations spread out across the gym floor, four treadmills, two rowing machines (a few more are coming soon), group-treadmill workouts, free weights and a fall/winter aerobics program with an instructor three times per week. Plus, members can use the center two days per week, come as often or infrequently they want, drop in classes at any time during their chosen schedule period or participate in event groups.
Corus distinguishes itself by integrating music into workouts and providing choir experiences, unlike other gyms.
Eric Goffman, the gym director and sole full-time manager, emphasizes that they have provided much more than just equipment, stating: "We've ensured we offer items beyond basic equipment. "We have a great variety of instruments; we have vocal training with professional musicians who work here part-time."
Goffman keeps up with guest artists including Patsy Cline, Whoopi Goldberg, Billy Preston and Ray Charles as well as performing bands like the Supremes, Frank Sinatra and Louis Armstrong.
For example, chorus groups will join in regular free-weight set-up sessions and there will be daily sessions involving singing while doing various exercises like sit-ups and crunches. And they'll all do it tied together by a common theme such as holiday songs, rhythm-and-blend songs, original choruses -- even some technical terms like balladeer, madrigalists, chorus masters, etc.
Instead of letting people walk around aimlessly, Goffman said he encourages them to sing and dance with friends as long as it is within the actual working area of the gym and no two people ever try to hit each other over the head.
Staff at the gym organize workshops by staff members, focusing on helping individuals maximize their learning techniques through open forums. Because of limited space, instructors may limit classes to seven to nine individuals so as not to overwhelm anyone.
Members must pay separately for lessons, although Goffman said future plans include funding available hours for those wanting either private instruction or group instruction.
There is a waiting list if you're looking for classes. However, if you already know what type of class you'd like to have done, Goffman said up to six members could attend, depending on availability. Lessons can be reserved individually or through group bookings but, due to scheduling, Goffman said a member needing private time would always have to wait until someone else does not need to take his or her place.

The National September 11 Memorial & Museum is open every day from 9 a.m. until 5 p.m., except Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, and Christmas Day.
Visitors, dressed in white shirts with blue sleeves or black pants, took turn stepping into the middle of the wide chasm created by that tragic attack more than 13 years ago.
Thousands of others crowded around benches and chairs positioned along the walkway leading toward the memorial. A few hundred walked up the path to sit on stone steps surrounding both pools; some built makeshift seating out of cardboard boxes and other recyclables; some left notes inside small gift bags.
Among them was Ying He, whose son died two days after the attacks at age 13.
"He's buried now but he wanted to get back to me," said her mother, Ling Young. "He always says: 'Mommy, if I don't go back to heaven, could you give me a little time?'
Opened on June 30, the museum showcases four exhibition levels that explore the history of terror attacks by depicting the destruction of the Twin Towers.
Each level includes interactive exhibits focused on what people experienced that dreadful morning, including video footage, photos, letters and audio from family members who survived or lost loved ones there. Informational markers near each exhibit provide an historical context for how they felt during their experience.
Five-floor units each feature their own secluded garden. The walls are covered in hand-painted images showing the memorials across the country commemorating that horrible moment when planes were flown into the World Trade Centers and the Pentagon on that horrific morning 13 years ago, Tuesday at 8 am, local time.
One wall's painting of this scene originally painted by then-United Nations Ambassador David Scheffer hangs over his grave outside the cemetery next door to his home in downtown Manhattan.
What's more touching, though it's probably understandable, is one of the illustrations that portrays the aftermath of those events — leaving behind a memorial-filled street littered with leftover food containers and boxes and bottles of soda cans as survivors scrounge for money for water.
Volunteers from the nonprofit Replicore provide yellow capsules that visitors can use to enter special rooms, where their names are recorded in memory near the end of the journey.

get hold of one... In fact, it was pretty obvious from the beginning just how difficult, dangerous and stupid it would be for me to run this bike in any way other than I'm already used to here.
You see, as you can imagine I have a bit of cycling experience (and love my mountain bike) but let's face it the only real riding hobby I've ever had is motorcycling! So after years using two different KTM machines prior to stepping into the unknown world of road-bikes or even electric bikes I needed a "vehicle" which could handle what I'd call steeper roads... So if there is one thing I know about riding on gravel/paved roads then it's that they aren't meant for an agile and fast machine!
It took me less time (a few weeks!) to learn how to ride on gravel than anyone else has managed to do simply by judging things like speed/torque/speed etc - particularly when it came to changing from sport-riding mode to a more aggressive touring position. And although I now understand better how these machines are engineered I don't really think too many riders out there will immediately realise this transition.
With its width-to-height ratio (just over 3/5ths) the new CB1100 looks every inch the "big-bike". Although the front end does look rather racy with the slim waistline and lightening-like rim set-up perhaps a little more finesse might help convince those looking to get behind the wheel... And although I believe the handling characteristics have been altered somewhat in line with the other bikes in this class I don't think they're necessarily much better after their recent changes. Perhaps I'm being unfair to the engineers at Honda; after all following so much of what I have done up to date on the new 2014 models is based upon the fact that they're very robust designs which take minimal effort to operate. I'm sure most manufacturers would say the same thing about their latest models!
This model has slightly broader dimensions compared to several smaller Honda models, though the actual difference in size might be minimal given the minor variations among chassis sizes. I'm not sure if they really intended this change as it seems a shame given the overall aesthetic design but more on that later...
The rear brake system is essentially identical to that found on the old model Honda bikes while the front brakes still use a 3-piston caliper fitted along side a single disc - presumably for versatility reasons. However, despite having similar proportions it seems the front brake system doesn't fit quite right so makes a tiny amount of squeaking noise under certain conditions. Also interestingly the brake lever fits slightly further forward than previous models so the brake pad assembly will need a little adjustment before it's ready for first use. My initial thought was that maybe unused carbon pads were making things a little worse than expected but they didn't seem to present any issues until I eventually replaced them once more fully adjusted

who died last week. Larry King, a former KFMB-TV ("KFI") news anchor and CBS News correspondent, expressed gratitude for being honored by partnering with Ronni over numerous years.
A true innovator, Ronni pioneered new business strategies when he launched The Hollywood Exchange. He created an Internet-based directory that enabled businesses to publicly list their profiles in a searchable database and create customized websites to attract potential clients. This innovative service now has more than 45,000 users worldwide – including Fortune 500 companies like Intel and Verizon Communications as well as diverse groups such as real estate firms and travel agencies – all utilizing the service.
Ronni founded the first Federal Direct Mail Advertising Agency Association Inc. The organization grew to be among the largest and most prestigious in print advertising due to its national membership of over 300 agencies.
In his early years as an independent agent, Ronni had remarkable success by building a roster of corporate clients ranging from IBM to Coca-Cola and bringing them national attention, primarily in trade publications. During this time, Ronni partnered with NBC Television Network president James Burke, resulting in some highly publicized successes, most notably capturing the highest-rated drama series at prime-time television, General Hospital, and winning the Emmy award for Outstanding Programmanship following the network's production of General Hospital for eleven consecutive seasons.
Alongside Burke, Ronni coordinated the successful launch of TV Guide magazine and later founded the Media Association Foundation, whose mission is to help support the journalism profession within the U.S. Today, Ronni continues to serve on the Board of Directors of the Media Association Foundation, helping guide it forward in its efforts to advance the value of quality journalism throughout America.
In addition to his work in television broadcasting, Ronni excelled at managing personal appearances for films and television shows, acting as an agent for prominent actors and directors during both studio presentations and live tours.
When he wasn't busy serving as director of publicity for his own company or providing representation for others, Ronni found enjoyment in operating his successful restaurant, La Paloma Fandango in Los Feliz, where he managed the kitchen staff and supervised all aspects of food preparation.
One of his proudest professional achievements came in 1987, when he organized an event honoring Howard Stern at Cineplex Odeon and the Motion Picture Association of America in Los Angeles, marking the beginning of "The Festival of Freedom," the world’s premier open forum on freedom of expression and censorship. Through Ronni’s firm commitment, organizations like Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, Freedom House, Center For Public Justice, Independent Voices Action Fund and the American Civil Liberties Union helped make the proceedings free speech events truly representative of the values shared by each organization.
This November marked the commencement of Ronni's funeral services at Butner Chapel & Mortuary, LA and the viewing hours are currently being scheduled. Services will take place Dec. 13 at 3 p.m.

user interactions in our modern world have become almost seamless; it's second nature for us to interact with the internet, online services, and other digital platforms without even realizing what we are doing when it comes to controlling these systems. We hardly notice that familiar mouse movements or touch gestures will automate simple tasks (like clicking a "Done" button after filling out an interactive form) while keeping our fingers busy by navigating through notifications or reading tweets.
This state of affairs has created some interesting questions about human-computer interaction – specifically, if we're capable of making meaningful progress with intuitively designed interfaces built using unnatural methods like typing text into fields or flicking through panes. I will examine my own experiences as a user interface designer to determine if there are still opportunities for enhancing computer interaction design in the current era. I'll talk about two new technologies: VR headsets that allow you to literally 'walk' inside graphics screens, alongside a case study from the customer service industry, sharing insights about why translating real-world experiences into virtual reality can impact outcomes dramatically.
Quick recap:
Moment of Truth
In his seminal research paper entitled Moment of Truth, Ulrich Klemm discussed three factors involved when completing a task within an application:
- Task Effectiveness - Is your task effectively completed?
Are you satisfied with the ease of use of your product?
Klemm highlights six key stages in his method for conducting open-ended task tests: Phase One—Awareness & Exploration (Contextualization). Here, subjects find themselves in a scenario without predefined guidelines yet required to achieve their designated objectives within the allotted time frame.
Browser: Google's Chrome. Once opened, users enter into self-guided exploration mode to discover various features and functions available within the program. Users may browse websites around the internet, watch videos via YouTube Live, access social media accounts, etc.

|List of items were shown, added item to cart||Easy|
Phase Two - Retrieving Knowledge
Next is retrieving skills necessary to accomplish the objective/task which require actions interacting with the environment directly rather than simply looking around and browsing through options.

Our contemporary society has made user interactions highly automatic; virtually unnoticed, we navigate through the internet, utilize online services, and engage with various digital interfaces, largely unaware of how they operate. We hardly notice that familiar mouse movements or touch gestures will automate simple tasks (like clicking a "Done" button after filling out an interactive form) while keeping our fingers busy by navigating through notifications or reading tweets.
This state of affairs has created some interesting questions about human-computer interaction – specifically, if we're capable of making meaningful progress with intuitively designed interfaces built using unnatural methods like typing text into fields or flicking through panes. I will examine my own experiences as a user interface designer to determine if there are still opportunities for enhancing computer interaction design in the current era. I'll talk about two new technologies: VR headsets that allow you to literally 'walk' inside graphics screens, alongside a case study from the customer service industry, sharing insights about why translating real-world experiences into virtual reality can impact outcomes dramatically.

What Are Skin Tags?
As mentioned above, these little buggers stand out in some unfortunate spots. When they appear around the eyes, mouth or neck, they tend to be particularly embarrassing because they often pop up under the chin, right by those very same features. They also look pretty ugly anywhere else on your body!
Although skin tags themselves aren't really a huge concern, they do require some attention from the dermatology world. Details on various aspects of skin tags are provided below...
Why People Develop Them
A skin tag is a small growth that forms at the junction of your eyelids, just below your throat line, behind your earlobe, over chest hair or in any other area where new blood vessels are pushing through the tissue covering the surface layers. It appears as a fleshy bump on the outer layer of your skin. These bumps don't really grow fast and may stay the same size throughout your life; however, they could shrink as older folks lose volume. In fact, the American Academy of Dermatology suggests using lubricant to help prevent rubbing away too much skin underneath them as well as dressing them with loose-fitting clothes so they aren't accidentally pulled down.
Where Do They Appear Most Typically?
Skin tags frequently develop in regions subjected to friction (for example, on the arms after exercise) or areas lacking substantial skin coverage (such as inner lip folds or ear creases). However, they also occur more commonly on hairy areas like the back of your head, nape of your neck, thighs & abdomen due to friction between hairs & skin cells. Finally! If you experience excessive itching/skintightness on unprotected parts of your body such as outermost edges of breasts while bathing regularly enough you might want consider having this reviewed by your physician since sometimes these sorts of symptoms indicate presence another condition called Paget’s disease of bone which causes abnormal growths along nerves found deep within bones making bones more flexible than normal.
How Should You Treat Them At Home?
Most people notice their skin tags early in life and there is no scientific consensus regarding whether they develop before birth or later in childhood but many experts estimate that one third develop during infancy—more specifically during first six months following birth until 3 years old—and another 20% develop between ages six to seven months and eight years old (though there is evidence suggesting that they may last longer). Freezing or burning them using liquid nitrogen or electric needles is a straightforward treatment method. Another method entails cutting them into smaller pieces then removing individual drops individually rather than trying to pluck whole ones at once thereby avoiding the pain

This month we look at things a business needs to know when advertising with Newbridge College.
There are two types of ads, information and commercial. Both need to follow certain guidelines.
To advertise one-on-one with someone — such as a student or prospective parent — use “personal” information, which tells who you are, why you’re interested in meeting them, where you live and a quote or number to contact the person being advertised to.
Consider beginning your research at chooseadvertising.com or adweek.com.
If you have more than one person wanting to be contacted — say you’re looking for sponsors for an event or program — send out a press release or news story. Include all details of what you’re offering (when), to whom and other important facts in larger print size.
When you do determine a budget amount, check with the publisher whether there is an annual fee. Some publishers reserve the right to decline ads with large budgets reserved specifically for major advertisers.
All agencies must obtain approval of their advertising plans prior to publishing any advertisement. To publish under one date, multiple advertisements are permitted if they appear in both English and Spanish. If multiple publishers are utilized during the translation process, advertisements pertaining to full bilingual status shall be permitted under a single date pattern. Board room ads: One-half cent ($1/hour) per square foot.
All newly established agencies posting classified ads are granted two complimentary articles per month, regardless of their preferred language (either English or Spanish).

No advertiser guarantees anything beyond providing good content and making attractive ads. What was advertised on ads yesterday and tomorrow will not guarantee success for January sales.

The rates are managed based on the agency's experience levels.

It depends on how long the announcement was going

Now, parts of central Mass are being targeted.
"We have to be mindful that they're here," said Marni Kirschbaum, a USDA entomologist who heads up the beetle eradication program.
Kirschbaum contends that a significant portion of Massachusetts harbors pests due to their prevalence in eastern Canada, where predators are ineffective at managing the beetle's population.
"It would probably be pretty much widespread now if we didn't do anything else [against it]," she noted.
There are two types of Asian longhorned beetles, Kirschbaum notes. One is good and the other bad, meaning not all can be controlled. Both give off a distinctive buzzing sound when disturbed. Their preference lies in using hardwoods.
When Michigan lost its entire population of Asian longhorn beetles due to mass killings by professional insect controllers, Kirschbaum notes "that was only partially possible."
"Our best bet is going to be [using] natural controls like birds or native species" which account for about half of the total number released into the area surrounding Worcester. Kirschbaum anticipates that bird populations will rise when the beetle population diminishes. Another 75 percent will die out without help, she adds. More than one-fourth of the treated insects perished when there was no wind to blow them away.
"There are so many factors involved that any given situation may have mixed outcomes," says Kirschbaum.
She mandates that anyone discovering a damaged tree, particularly within 10 feet of highway entrances, should notify authorities promptly before disposing of the wood to prevent further spread of infestations.
Trays containing powder and water make it possible to spray the trees automatically, rather than causing damage to human life and property.
"The 'insecticides' used in our work...are approved for use against these specific pests by the Environmental Protection Agency, though materials registered to combat other problematic beetles are sometimes used to treat these species." says Kirschbaum, whose team includes James Bierlein, a consultant with Beech Tree Pest Management.
In June, Kirschbaum predicts that new infestations of Asian longhorn beetles will come from the west instead of east.

To understand why, let’s look at how this all started: PG&E shut down 30-40 wind turbines off the coast of San Francisco Bay, near the Marin Headlands, in September 2016 because they were tumbling out of balance or coming close to falling over on violent gusts known as “gust-forces.” While installing the turbine above ground, they closed a small gap created by the turbine that broke apart in an earthquake six years prior. Because these two problems were unrelated issues, they didn’t expect either fixed by putting back one of the three damaged turbines – which they did in January 2017 after consulting with experts. However, instead of installing the new turbine immediately, they waited until late November to finish construction and place their last turbine into service, meaning they didn’t perform basic tests using computer models to ensure the system would stabilize under a range of wind conditions. Shortly after, the system malfunctioned once more.
This time the system fell, hitting and destroying nearby buildings. Reports indicate that six individuals sustained injuries, with concerns about potential disappearances. Additionally, the incident caused significant property damage amounting to $9 million, including the sinking of a boat. When Geraldo Rivera reported the story live on TV recently, he told the audience: “It has just become clear to us that we need to protect our coastline not with concrete but by restoring nature” — which is true since the ruined turbines destroyed vegetation critical for shorelines protecting houses from rising seas and stronger storms.
The result has been lawsuits filed against both state regulators and the company itself charging millions per claim. Since PG&E offers insurance coverage for its customers affected, they could theoretically file suit even if they weren't covered themselves, though others might argue that's unfair given that PG&E insured them only up to certain limits. Some also point to recent accolades given to BP for being fined billions more dollars for causing even worse damage during hurricane Katrina than PG&E’s 2016 storm, despite knowing full well what was going to happen based on past experiences.
PG&E CEO Darryl Morey called it “a victimless tragedy” while Berkeley city councilwoman Beth Gould said she believes laws should require utility companies like his own not to operate wind farms so close to populated areas without first conducting proper seismic analysis before deciding whether those sites pose significant dangers worth the risks associated with placing infrastructure along such fragile shores. Both received immediate backlash, however, from within industry circles including several lawmakers who criticized them as corporate chauvinists trying to get away with letting their employees die instead of spending enough money now preventing future disasters.
When confronted directly about her decision not to take legal action following BP's actions mentioned above, Governor Jerry Brown famously replied:
"You know, it looks bad... But nobody gets paid twice!"

First of all, our favorite wines are an expression of terrior. Yes, climate definitely has an impact on what we taste in wine — but so does soil, micro-climate (including water), geological profile of the area, slope or aspect of vineyard location and other factors such as elevation.
Local winemakers have tasted their grapes over many years, discovering how best they respond to certain elements including particular wines from regions, soils and varieties grown throughout different seasons. We should expect them to be aware of these things as well because even today professional winemakers still sample regularly for quality, consistency and flavor, testing under similar conditions each year and checking notes made 10-20 years ago to keep track of changes in character (or lack of same).
So why do we look just to temperature? When I first started buying wine in college and later in graduate school I was told my palate wouldn’t mature until I got older and more experienced. Gradually this became a recipe for ignoring warming temperatures in favor of colder ones. Exceptions occurred frequently; many people know friends who hale from Washington State yet prefer either Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, or Chardonnay over other varieties. The biggest issue with relying on vintage alone for choosing a new beverage type, particularly when someone is younger, lies in avoiding a situation where their taste buds become accustomed to flavors they haven't appreciated previously.
What can be done about this aesthetic bias towards cooler climates? First try grasping that there really aren’t any “seasonal” grapes or styles. Green and blue hues may be associated with summer colors and warm feelings; reds symbolize passion and intensity. Wines made from springtime or early summer grapes tend to be cool-toned while those fermented in September will display warmer tones thanks to ripened grapes.
Reflect on autumn leaves when you ponder the impact of the oak tree. Autumn coloration means more oxygen is present, resulting in lighter oak flavors. During winter, oak tannins develop faster. Finally, take into account differences in fruit timing and quantity, which greatly influences final wine composition. Temperatures play a role here too, affecting sugar levels.
Options for choosing between weather and wine include utilizing fruit's maturity rather than its vintage. It refers to maturities achieved through aging in barrels rather than fermentation dates;
• Vintage is evaluated partially by maturity and partly by variety;
• Grape variety is considered more as an identifier than actual indicator of quality.
There is also an argument that certain varietals express better characteristics during specific times of year depending on growing conditions. Most winemakers use identical grape varieties across diverse regions, rendering them equally advantageous regardless of seasonal timing.

, Coke plans to launch two test tubes carrying its signature beverage on an unmanned rocket Monday (Jan. 30) while Pepsi will hitchhike aboard a separate rocket for its experiments.
